why: '3 a.m.' is relatable, but '这句' points to a sentence the subtitles never show. What really keeps me is #3 at 6-9 s: a clay tablet and Harvard giving the same answer is an odd pair, and I want to see how it works out.
first_moment_I_got_curious: #3 (6.47 s) 「泥板上的答案，和[哈佛]一样」; the curiosity becomes an open loop at #10 (41.56 s) 「她后面的话，[留到最后]」
where_I_would_swipe_away: 9.25-16.66 s: 7.4 s with no subtitle right after the hook promises an answer
82-92 s (#20-21 Nietzsche): fourth famous quote in a row, starts to feel like a 名人名言串烧 (quote medley); only the #10 loop keeps me
135.11-140.86 s: 5.75 s gap after #32, which sounds like the ending, so I'd miss the hotpot line
46-56 s (#11-13 Confucius), lower risk: I know it from school, feels like a textbook
lines_I_did_not_understand: #1 这句: which sentence? Never shown in the subtitles
#4 一个无名诗人: where and when? I assumed he wrote the clay tablet, then Gilgamesh appears and I lost track of which text is the tablet
#2 vs #32: 近四千年前 vs 三千多年前, which is it?
#14 只差30票: then what? The line never says he was executed
#17-19: the quote comes before the speaker, the emperor is never named, and 管着帝国的人 leaves me asking which empire
#18 做一个人该做的事: sounds deep, means nothing concrete
#24 妻子已经不在了: what am I supposed to take from it? Cuts to Harvard after 1.8 s
#26 他们原以为，50岁的胆固醇更要紧: who are 'they'? Clumsy wording, had to read it twice
#27 看的是关系: my first reading was guanxi (走关系, pulling strings), not relationships
#31 人的命运: fate, or the thing humans are supposed to do?
#33 「你也没睡？明天吃火锅！」: same brackets as the historical quotes; who is speaking?
takeaway_in_my_words: For 4,000 years people have asked whether life is worth it at 3 a.m. The oldest answer and Harvard's 80-year study say the same thing: the people close to you.
surprise_that_stuck: Frankl got through the camp on his wife's face and only learned afterwards that she was already dead (#24). Runner-up: the emperor who didn't want to get up either (#19).
